widgets_values:
Generate a three-panel storyboard (triptych) composition in a single image.
The image must be clearly divided into three distinct frames with visible panel borders, spacing, or frame lines.
All three panels must be fully visible at the same time.

Using the provided image as the primary reference, first analyze and infer the main subject, theme, and any implied contrast or duality.

Within each panel, reinterpret the inferred theme as a high-quality isometric miniature 3D parallel-world diorama, depicting two contrasting realities of the same subject (World A vs World B).

Each panel must explore a different compositional solution.
Do not repeat the same layout, split direction, or spatial logic across panels.
Allow varied approaches such as:
– diagonal or curved reality divisions  
– layered or offset depth structures  
– foreground–background separation  
– fragmented, stepped, or transitioning bases  
– partial overlaps between realities  

Preserve identity, proportions, and visual coherence across panels, but allow camera framing and internal structure to change from panel to panel.

Apply soft refined textures, realistic PBR materials, and miniature-scale diorama craftsmanship in all panels.
Use clearly contrasting lighting styles, color grading, atmosphere, or environmental cues between World A and World B within each panel, varying emphasis across the three frames.

Include tiny stylized human characters in every panel, without facial details, existing differently in each reality.
Use a clean solid background color behind the entire three-panel composition.

At the top-center of the full image (not inside individual panels), display a concise title derived from the inferred subject,
beneath it place the subtitle “Parallel Realities”,
and optionally include a minimal abstract icon.
Ensure all text automatically adapts to background contrast (white or black).

Maintain a cinematic, high-end miniature diorama aesthetic with clear depth, consistent scale, and strong visual rhythm across the three panels.
Avoid symmetry, duplication, or predictable repetition; each panel should feel like a distinct yet related interpretation of the same idea.
